observations.finding: DNA (blue/DAPI) signal in nuclei is visibly dimmer/paler in both treated fields versus bright saturated blue nuclei in DMSO control under identical contrast. Consistent with provided measurement nuc_dna_mean z=-12.7 (0.33 vs DMSO 0.49).

Cell footprint visibly larger and more spread with broad red F-actin lamellipodia/green tubulin cytoplasm in treated fields; cells more dispersed in f_a8ffb3ece708 and large polygonal in f_d2b639371bc9 versus compact DMSO colonies. Consistent with cell_area z=6.08 (5039 vs 4020) and cell_major_axis z=5.75 (110 vs 96) and cell_nuc_area_ratio z=4.87 (5.92 vs 4.78).

Nuclei appear slightly enlarged in long axis, smooth oval contours, without fragmentation, micronuclei or multinucleation. Consistent with nuc_major_axis z=5.45 (38.6 vs 36.8) and nuc_solidity z=4.92 (0.974 vs 0.973).

Fewer bright condensed yellow-white mitotic-like figures: DMSO shows ~3-4 per field, treated shows 0 in f_a8ffb3ece708 (one dim orange debris) and ~2 faint in f_d2b639371bc9. Consistent with frac_mitotic_like z=-3.77 (0.0 vs 0.015).
Cell shape not markedly more elongated; treated cells appear similarly polygonal/rounded with slight decrease in elongation versus DMSO, consistent with cell_eccentricity z=-4.07 (0.764 vs 0.789).

Beta-tubulin (green) filamentous network and F-actin (red) peripheral stress fibers/cortical staining remain intact in treated fields, no collapse, bundling, or diffuse loss seen comparable to DMSO. No measurement for tubulin/actin intensity or organization was provided.

Overall confluence variable: f_a8ffb3ece708 sparser with gaps, f_d2b639371bc9 dense similar to DMSO; no massive cell loss or apoptotic fragmentation apparent. No measurement for cell count per field was provided (only total cells_measured=156).

report.uncertainty: high uncertainty on MoA from composites alone; phenotype is mainly reduced DAPI intensity with larger spread cells and G-phase-like arrest, without cytoskeletal collapse or mitotic arrest. No supporting evidence for microtubule, actin, or Aurora/Eg5 mitotic phenotypes in these composites; DNA replication/damage or protein synthesis/degradation cannot be distinguished without additional markers, so unknown is most appropriate.

data.note:
Note: Specimen s_826e117c63 unblinded as methotrexate (PubChem 126941, ChEMBL CHEMBL34259 DHFR inhibitor per e18), BBBC021 annotated DNA replication. My conclusion Protein degradation (p=0.38) was incorrect per code.

Reflection: All 4 wells showed extreme nuc_dna_mean z≈-12, increased cell_area/nuc_major_axis and loss of mitotic figures, but no tubulin/actin collapse (e2,e3,e5,e9,e10). Atlas similarity was low (0.31-0.40) and NSC vote split 2 Protein degradation /1 DNA damage /1 DNA replication (e11), with initial 2/2 Protein degradation driven by proteasome inhibitors ALLN/MG-132 (e4). I over-weighted that plurality despite phenotypic clues of antifolate S-phase/G1 arrest - reduced DAPI intensity and enlarged spread cells - which aligns with DHFR inhibition depleting tetrahydrofolate/dTMP and inhibiting DNA synthesis.

PubChem/ChEMBL confirm DHFR inhibitor (e18). Literature supports mechanism: Methotrexate and Pralatrexate review (PMID 26433846) and antifolate resistance/DHFR amplification reviews (PMID 17333344, PMID 40088855) describe DHFR as target leading to impaired DNA replication; early replication intermediate study in methotrexate-resistant cells (PMID 3006761) also links it to DNA replication stress. Potency at 0.003µM (e10) and flat dose-response (e12-e13) should have favored DNA replication over proteasome phenotype despite morphological similarity.

reflection.text:
This was a best-estimate call on a saturated phenotype that was incorrect: submitted Protein degradation 0.38 vs truth DNA replication (methotrexate, dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor, e17/e18). Mechanism as DHFR inhibitor depleting reduced folates for thymidylate and purine synthesis and therefore DNA replication is supported by the unblinding literature PMID 26433846, PMID 17333344, PMID 40088855. 

What the evidence got right: 
Acquisition excluded cytoskeletal/mitotic MoAs correctly. e2 (0.1 uM, 141 cells: nuc_dna_mean z -11.6, area +7.1, maj axis +5.4), e3 (3 uM, 156 cells: dna -12.7, area +6.1, maj axis +5.7), e9 (1 uM, 213 cells: dna -11.7, eccentricity -8.5, area +5.6) and e10 (0.003 uM, 161 cells: dna -12.9, area +8.0, maj axis +4.5) were all consistent: very low DAPI intensity, enlarged spread cells, low density vs DMSO but intact actin/tubulin with frac_mitotic_like constant across 4 wells e13, so e15 correctly down-weighted Microtubule stabilizers/destabilizers 0.05/0.02, Actin disruptors 0.02, Aurora 0.04 and Eg5 0.003, and e5 explicitly stated candidates: none. That part was appropriate.

What misled and what was missed:
1. Early anchoring on 2 wells. Initial compare_to_reference_atlas e4 over e2+e3 was 2/2 Protein degradation NSC vote, k-neighbours Protein degradation 4/10, DNA replication 4/10, Microtubule stabilizers 1/10. That drove acquire_well strategy to fill middle/high doses (0.1, 3, 1 uM) before establishing a baseline. When we expanded to 4 wells, e11 became 2/4 Protein degradation plurality only, with k-neighbours 3/10 Protein degradation, 2/10 DNA replication, 2/10 DNA damage. The per-well protocol truth shows why: w_f96481b907 0.1uM nearest Protein degradation sim 0.386, w_65f193b525 3uM Protein degradation sim 0.312, w_e171482d14 1uM nearest DNA damage sim 0.40, w_3ee65d4a02 0.003uM nearest DNA replication sim 0.351. The vote was split 2-1-1, summed similarities low 0.31-0.40, indicating poor and tied matches. Majority vote plurality is not majority.

2. Phenotype is non-discriminative for this atlas representation. e5 microscopist noted density lower but could not separate Protein degradation from DNA replication/DNA damage/Protein synthesis. e2/e3/e9/e10 pattern - deep dna reduction + increased area/eccentricity/major axis - was seen in all three top k-neighbour classes e11. This matches expectation for a potent antifolate where S-phase inhibition leads to reduced DNA synthesis signal, enlarged G1/S-arrested cells and lower count without mitotic block, but the same morphometric vector mapped to proteasome-related neighbours in this cell line/timepoint.

3. Dose-response added no discrimination due to acquisition choice. e6-e8 required >=3 wells and was uninformative with 2 wells. With 4 wells, e12 nuc_dna_mean rho +0.20 p=0.8 and e14 cell_area rho -0.80 p=0.2 were flat/non-significant because even the lowest available dose e10 0.003 uM was already saturated at z -12.9 / +8.0. We spent budget to reach 0/4 wells left e1,e11 without ever sampling below saturation to obtain an EC50 or a trend that separates G1 arrest (DNA replication) from proteotoxic swelling. All four wells were single replicates, so no variance estimate.

Confidence was appropriately low 0.38 with 0.22 DNA replication and 0.18 DNA damage residual in e15/e16, and review correctly approved as justified best estimate given exhausted budget. The error was over-interpreting a 2/4 plurality from early unanimous neighbours when e5 and e11 explicitly flagged mixed neighbours and flat dose-response. No PMID in this run directly linked methotrexate morphology to reduced DAPI/G1 enlargement; e19 returned 5 hits, e20 returned 0 hits, so literature did not rescue.

Next time with this budget I would acquire the lowest dose first to find EC50, include replicates rather than 4 singletons across saturated doses, and not submit on NSC alone when e5 says visual candidates: none and similarities <0.4 - requiring orthogonal DNA synthesis/ cell cycle assay (EdU/flow) as proposed, not proteasome biochemistry alone.
